correctness.rationale: For every two-dimensional dihedral irreducible, in the normalized Pauli basis the orbit projectors have scalar coordinate 1/sqrt(2), and their three Bloch coordinates have zero mean. Summing q^j yields the identity eigenvalue n and exactly three nonnegative traceless eigenvalues, with a separate computation for q=-1; their sum is n. This proves the sharp n/3 bound and the exact equality loci. At equality the frame superoperator acts as n(X+tr(X)I)/3, proving the projective 2-design identity. The standalone verifier constructs projectors directly and reproduced 588 spectra and 196 optimal examples; finite tests supplement, not replace, the exact proof. Unweighted full group orbit, unit generators and precise Hermitian domain are explicit.

value.rationale: For a structured family of group-generated phaseless measurements, the smallest operator-frame eigenvalue controls the worst-case linear matrix-inversion error, a meaningful quantity not addressed by qualitative phase-retrieval rank alone. The result completely classifies optimal generators for every two-dimensional irrep of every finite dihedral group, establishes attainment of the global tight-design optimum, and isolates the single representation type where a nonreal relative phase is essential. It gives exact design options and a sharp real-generator obstruction, without claiming a new universal 2-design theorem or nonlinear noise guarantees.
